curriculum.title: Mission from Jerusalem to the Nations

core.big_idea: The Spirit-directed mission crossed geographic, ethnic, and social boundaries.

passages.reading_note: Read in immediate context; select age-appropriate portions without changing the claim.

core.metanarrative_position: Apostolic mission: Mission within the Church, Worship, and Mission cycle

claims.statement: Acts 1:8 frames the witness of Jesus' followers as expanding from Jerusalem outward.
Acts 8 narrates gospel movement through persecution and Philip's encounter with an Ethiopian official, while Acts 13 depicts the Antioch church sending Barnabas and Saul.
Acts presents mission as crossing geographic, ethnic, and social boundaries under the Spirit's direction.

core.interpretation_skill: Observe text; reconstruct context; account for genre; distinguish text, synthesis, inference, and application

learning.foundation_objective: Analyse the relevant text and explain the case that the spirit-directed mission crossed geographic, ethnic, and social boundaries.
learning.extension_objective: Test the claim against context, genre, canonical synthesis, credible alternatives, and the limits of the available evidence.
know: The Spirit-directed mission crossed geographic, ethnic, and social boundaries.
The lesson belongs in Apostolic mission.
understand: Direct observation must remain distinct from interpretation, synthesis, framework position, and application.
practise: Classify each major claim by evidence type.
State one credible interpretive limit or alternative before application.
become: A learner who reads Scripture carefully and responds with faithful trust, wisdom, worship, service, and love.
success_evidence: Student can summarize the selected passage.
Student can support the big idea with evidence.
Student can distinguish observation from interpretation or application.

Acts 8 narrates gospel movement through persecution and Philip's encounter with an Ethiopian official, while Acts 13 depicts the Antioch church sending Barnabas and Saul.
interpretation_notes: Start with the selected passage before moving to synthesis or application.

theological_guardrails: Do not equate mission with cultural domination. Acts repeatedly portrays the gospel crossing boundaries rather than requiring ethnic assimilation.
Questions and disagreement may be expressed without embarrassment or coercion.

family.title: Pentecost and the Church's Public Beginning
family.parent_intro: This week we are revisiting Mission from Jerusalem to the Nations. Keep the focus on what Acts 1:8; 8:4-40; 13:1-3 actually says and one faithful response.

flow.instructions: Connect Mission from Jerusalem to the Nations to the story already learned in Church, Worship, and Mission.
Read a manageable selection from Acts 1:8; 8:4-40; 13:1-3 and name direct observations.
Restate the big idea in your own words: The Spirit-directed mission crossed geographic, ethnic, and social boundaries.
Use Mission from Jerusalem to the Nations Claim Audit verbally or on paper.
Name one concrete faithful response for this week.

questions: What does the passage directly say?
What is one response we can practise?

interactive.title: Pentecost and the Church's Public Beginning Claim Audit
interactive.instructions: Use the Mission from Jerusalem to the Nations Claim Audit orally or on paper to sort direct observations from interpretations and responses.

family.weekly_action: Choose one concrete response connected to the spirit-directed mission crossed geographic, ethnic, and social boundaries and practise it this week.
family.prayer: Thank God for what is clear in the passage; ask for wisdom to respond faithfully without claiming more than the text supports.
family.parent_note: Questions are welcome. Do not force disclosure, certainty, public prayer, baptism, or another public religious decision.

quiz.question: Which passage is central to Mission from Jerusalem to the Nations?

quiz.question: Which reading habit is most responsible?
options: Observe context and genre before concluding.
Start with the application you want.
Treat every narrative detail as a command.

answer.text: Observe context and genre before concluding.

quiz.explanation: Observation and context precede synthesis and application.

quiz.question: Acts 1:8 frames the witness of Jesus' followers as expanding from Jerusalem outward.
quiz.explanation: This statement is supported directly by the lesson evidence.

quiz.question: Should an inference be described as explicit text when the passage does not state it directly?
quiz.explanation: Inference and direct wording must remain distinct.

accessibility.reading_level: Teen independent or guided close reading
accessibility.plain_language_rule: Define unfamiliar terms before theological shorthand.
neurodiversity_supports: Allow students to pass on personal-sharing questions.
non_reader_support: Read aloud and use icons, sequence cards, oral choices, or a scribe.

do_not_ask: Do not require disclosure of trauma, family finances, grief, or private spiritual decisions.
Do not pressure a child or young person toward baptism, public prayer, or another public response.
safeguarding.teacher_response: Use the lesson guardrails in the review sheet; answer from the evidence, avoid coercion, and route personal or safety concerns to appropriate adults.
